text:
jonathan (support): FYI customer Sam from AcmeMaps reporting a big throughput drop on their Dedicated pool dp-73 — lots of 429s and long queue latencies since ~09:12 UTC. sample error: "request throttled: batch too full"

maria (eng-runtime): thx. do we have autoscaler events or recent deploys for dp-73?

jonathan (support): no deploys. here's the timeline they sent: high tail latency spike at 09:11, 429 rate jumped from 0.2% -> 7% over 15m. they say traffic pattern unchanged. attaching short log paste: 
```
2026-03-16T09:11:03Z pool=dp-73 req_id=abc123 status=429 reason="batch_capacity_exceeded" tokens=3584
2026-03-16T09:11:04Z pool=dp-73 req_id=def456 status=200 latency_ms=732 tokens=7800
2026-03-16T09:11:10Z pool=dp-73 req_id=ghi789 status=429 reason="scheduler_reject" tokens=640
```

lee (sre): getting cluster metrics now. pinging autoscaler. @deploy-bot can you dump recent scaler events for dp-73?

deploy-bot: [auto] autoscaler: pool=dp-73 action=cooldown start=2026-03-16T09:10:50Z reason="oscillating_scale"
deploy-bot: [auto] autoscaler: pool=dp-73 scale_down from=8 to=6 at=2026-03-16T09:11:30Z

maria (eng-runtime): aha scale-down during the spike — that will amplify queueing. also saw some requests with huge token counts (7k-8k) that block batching. looks like token-based batching is starving smaller requests.

sam (acme-maps): we only saw normal user traffic — maybe one background job rotated a long prompt batch at 09:10. we can pause that if it helps.

lee (sre): quick mitigation steps: 1) pause/limit the background job (sam) 2) temporarily disable aggressive scale-down (increase cooldown) 3) cap per-request tokens at ingress to 4096 for this pool

maria (eng-runtime): agree. also change scheduler tuning: reduce continuous batching window and increase max_batch_tokens so single large requests don't force many small batches. current config snippet: 
```
scheduler:
  continuous_batching: true
  batching_window_ms: 10
  max_batch_size: 16
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  token_weighting: true
```

proposed quick-change: 
```
scheduler:
  continuous_batching: true
  batching_window_ms: 6
  max_batch_size: 24
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  per_request_token_cap: 4096
  enable_token_backpressure: true
```

jonathan (support): i'll tell the customer to pause that background job and confirm when done. any impact to latency from increasing max_batch_tokens?

maria (eng-runtime): slight potential tail increase for small requests but overall throughput should improve. we can canary the config on 2 nodes first.

ops-bot: [auto] applied temporary policy: pool=dp-73 per_request_token_cap=4096, autoscaler_min=6, autoscaler_cooldown_s=600 (canary on nodes n-12,n-13)

lee (sre): running smoke load test now with synthetic mix (20% large, 80% small) — baseline queued tokens/sec = 5500, after tune queued tokens/sec = 1800, 429 -> 0.6% so far.

maria (eng-runtime): good. next steps: 1) keep per-request cap in place 2) tune max_batch_tokens after analyzing distribution for 48h 3) add a scheduler metric alert for token-skew when >30% requests > 4k tokens 4) recommend customers throttle background large-batch jobs into off-peak windows

sam (acme-maps): paused job and seeing improvement on our side, thanks. will follow your guidance on breaking that job into smaller requests.

jonathan (support): marking escalated ticket as 'mitigated' pending 48h observation. will follow up with postmortem if token-skew recurs. :thumbsup:
